prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "colorize", with the standing line "Walks every black-and-white engraving cut from a historical book through one chosen colouring tool, keeping the book's ledger intact." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A folder of black-and-white engravings, with a ledger sheet on top, feeds a single line. The line passes one sheet at a time into a switching station with five labelled chutes, one per tool. Only one chute is open. The ledger sheet travels on a parallel track beside the images, untouched, and arrives at the same destination. The arrows run left to right, from the folder through the station to the output folder.

Magnified circles set beside it show The first circle shows a ledger line bearing a flag, with an engraving whose top stays uncoloured instead of turning blue sky. The second shows an engraving frame fitted to the nearest of nine accepted shapes, so its caption is not cropped away. The third shows four hands drawing sheets from one queue at once. The fourth shows two returned files, one JPEG and one PNG, each named by its true type. shows one engraving three ways: copied through, sepia-toned, and softly coloured.

Colour is used so that Soft Impressionist colour appears only on finished engravings and means the image was colourised. Ochre marks the ledger wherever it travels. A single red mark means a failed image that was skipped.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: Five tools in the switching station. Four workers by default for AI calls. Nine aspect shapes for Gemini framing. Two output destinations. One manifest in and one manifest out.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: manifest.yaml on the ledger sheet; --tool on the switching station; copy, ai, sepia, deoldify, and python-script on the five chutes; no_sky on the flagged ledger line; --workers on the four hands; --copy-to on the mirrored second folder; JPEG and PNG on the returned files; supporting folder on the output destination.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: manifest.yaml, extracted engravings, --tool, copy, ai, sepia, deoldify, python-script, image model, colorize prompt, credential store. no_sky, no blue sky, nearest aspect, --workers, JPEG, PNG. original, copied through, sepia tone, Impressionist palette. supporting folder, manifest copied, --copy-to, colorized images. extraction stage, failed image skipped, rerun to fill gaps, downstream stages.

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Default copy lets colour decisions wait; The ledger rides through unchanged. Flagged images get a sky-free prompt; For Gemini, framing matches the engraving; Filename follows the bytes returned; Parallel workers serve only AI calls. Lines and textures kept exactly as drawn. Mirrors results to a second folder. A failure is reported, never fatal.
